column1: # tools/i18n/glossary.tsv: nl phrase → Windows 11 en-GB phrase (notes/english-option-design.md §4.2), for the
# glossary rule of tools/i18n/check.py: when an nl text contains the phrase (longest first, at word boundaries),
# its en text must contain the English one. An error since the round-3 lock-in (R3-UI; check.py, check_ui.py,
# check_pairs.py; check_rust.py reads this file too). Columns: nl, en, flags ("name": case-sensitive).
# Where a second rendering is right (a progress form, Windows' own sentence, another sense of the word), a context
# row in tools/i18n/glossary-context.tsv names the places and the en phrase there; it is a separate file because
# check_rust.py takes every row of this one as a rule for the whole host.
# Rows the design marks "(check)" (Snelle instellingen, Batterijbesparing) and context-dependent words (Schijf:
# Disk or Drive; Info; Weergave; Afsluiten; Start: the menu or Verkenner's Home; Alles: the name or "everything") are
# left out on purpose; E0b's glossary report settles them. The en phrase may be inflected ("Format" in "Formatting").
# Windows Update (GW3, notes/claude/windows-update-gnome.md §8). "Opnieuw proberen": the round-3 lock-in (D-G41)
# keeps "Try again" (the 8 existing UI buttons) and gives the Update page Windows 11's "Retry" through a context row.
